item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Voyager One Against the References

turns.text: Make a silent 9-second widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1, using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Three equal-length scenes: 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Keep 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible. Show the probe near Earth, Jupiter, then Saturn; match its real dish-and-boom design. Don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

item.tests: Tests whether a factual film matches a named reference in dates, mission identity, spacecraft appearance and scene order.

answer_sheet.Facts to include: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and flew by Saturn in 1980.
answer_sheet.Length and scene order: 9 seconds total: three 3-second scenes showing Earth, Jupiter and Saturn in that order.
answer_sheet.Wording: Use exactly the five supplied labels. Keep Voyager 1 and Source: NASA Science visible throughout.
answer_sheet.Sound: Completely silent, with no narration, music or sound effects.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Your call, provided the spacecraft matches the real dish-and-boom design and the planets are recognizable.

must_haves: Three scenes appear in order, each lasting approximately three seconds: probe near Earth, near Jupiter, then near Saturn.
Each scene displays its corresponding date caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout.
The probe consistently has Voyager's large circular communications dish and projecting instrument booms, not solar-panel wings or a generic satellite body.
Jupiter is visibly banded and Saturn has prominent rings; neither is replaced with Uranus or Neptune.
The output contains no Uranus or Neptune flyby claims and no conflicting dates.

args.name: Voyager 1 — Earth, Jupiter, Saturn — Silent Facts

style.prompt: Create an exactly 9-second, completely silent widescreen educational fact clip about NASA's VOYAGER 1, not Voyager 2. Three scenes of exactly 3 seconds each, with hard cuts at 3.000s and 6.000s. Reference attribution: NASA Science, mission page https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Use the following supplied verified mission facts: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977; Jupiter flyby 1979; Saturn flyby 1980. Do not show or mention Uranus, Neptune, Voyager 2, or any other mission. Polished scientifically grounded CGI space visualization, recognizable planets, calm camera drift, crisp accessible infographic typography. Keep the SAME accurate Voyager spacecraft design across every shot: large white parabolic high-gain antenna dish, central compact metallic bus, long thin magnetometer boom, separate instrument science boom and radioisotope power-generator boom, delicate antenna rods; no solar panels, no fictional engines, no wings, no thruster exhaust. Spacecraft should be visible and distinct against space, with plausible proportions; planet sizes in composition may be illustrative rather than true scale. The ONLY five text strings allowed in the entire video are precisely these supplied labels, rendered with correct spelling and punctuation: 'Voyager 1', 'Source: NASA Science', 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Persistent title 'Voyager 1' at top left and persistent attribution 'Source: NASA Science' at bottom right must be fully visible in every frame from 0 through 9 seconds, in high contrast clean sans serif type inside safe margins. Each scene has exactly one additional large legible lower-left scene label, not overlapping the persistent attribution. 0.000–3.000 seconds: Voyager 1 in space near recognizable Earth, vivid blue oceans and white cloud patterns with curved sunlit limb; scene label exactly 'Launched: September 5, 1977'. 3.000–6.000 seconds: same spacecraft passing recognizable Jupiter, tan and cream cloud bands and Great Red Spot; replace the scene label instantly with exactly 'Jupiter flyby: 1979'. 6.000–9.000 seconds: same spacecraft near recognizable pale golden Saturn with prominent thin tilted rings; replace scene label instantly with exactly 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Persistent title and source do not change or disappear during cuts. No crossfades, no extra scenes, no end card, no extra text, no logos, no speech, no narration, no music, no sound effects, absolutely no audio.
